NEW SECTION . 15G.101 Definitions. 24 As used in this chapter, unless the context otherwise 25 requires: 26 1. “Board” means the same as defined in section 15.102. 27 2. “Entity” means an Iowa nonprofit organization established 28 to promote economic development and tourism in an area. 29 3. “Event” means a tourism-oriented athletic contest, 30 convention, music festival, or art festival. 31 4. “Financial assistance” means assistance provided only 32 from the funds, rights, and assets legally available to the 33 authority and includes but is not limited to assistance in the 34 form of grants. 35 -3- SF 660.2142 (2) 91 ns/js 3/ 10 5. “Fund” means the Iowa major events and tourism fund 1 established in section 15G.104. 2 6. “Program” means the Iowa major events and tourism program 3 established in section 15G.102. 4 Sec. 8. NEW SECTION . 15G.102 Iowa major events and tourism 5 program —— purpose. 6 1. The authority shall establish and administer the 7 Iowa major events and tourism program to provide financial 8 assistance to eligible entities that support events in this 9 state, or support events involving a geographic region that 10 includes this state, and the event generates large attendance, 11 significant publicity, and has a measurable economic impact on 12 this state. 13 2. The program shall be administered for the purpose of 14 awarding financial assistance to an eligible entity for any of 15 the following purposes: 16 a. To pay for or reimburse the costs incurred by the entity 17 to apply or bid for selection as the site for the event. 18 b. To pay for or reimburse the costs incurred by the entity 19 to plan or to conduct the event, including any fees charged by 20 a site selection organization as a prerequisite to hosting the 21 event, including but not limited to hosting fees, sanctioning 22 fees, participation fees, operational fees, or bid fees. 23 Sec. 9. NEW SECTION . 15G.103 Program —— application, 24 review, eligibility, and funding. 25 1. An application for financial assistance under the 26 program shall be submitted to the authority. For each 27 application that meets the eligibility criteria under 28 subsection 2, the authority shall conduct a staff evaluation 29 of the application and forward the application and staff 30 evaluation to the board. 31 2. a. The authority shall establish eligibility criteria 32 for the program by rule. The eligibility criteria must include 33 all of the following: 34 (1) The entity must currently be involved in the bidding and 35 -4- SF 660.2142 (2) 91 ns/js 4/ 10 selection process for the event for which the entity submits 1 an application. 2 (2) The entity’s application under subsection 1 must 3 include an economic analysis of the event that includes but is 4 not limited to all of the following: 5 (a) Projected hotel and motel room occupancies during the 6 event. 7 (b) Projected number of event attendees from this state, 8 other states, and other countries. 9 b. Notwithstanding paragraph “a” , an entity shall be deemed 10 eligible for the program if any of the following apply: 11 (1) After a highly competitive bidding and selection 12 process involving potential sites not located in this state, a 13 location in Iowa has been selected for the entity’s event. 14 (2) This state serves as the sole site for the entity’s 15 event. 16 (3) The sole site for the entity’s event is a geographical 17 region that includes this state and one or more contiguous 18 states. 19 3. When evaluating an application, the authority shall 20 consider, at a minimum, all of the following: 21 a. The potential impact of the event on the local, regional, 22 and state economies. 23 b. The event’s potential to attract visitors from this 24 state, other states, and other countries. 25 c. The amount of positive advertising or media coverage the 26 event may generate. 27 d. The quality, size, and scope of the event. 28 e. The ratio of public-to-private investment required for 29 the event. 30 4. a. (1) Upon review of the staff evaluation, the board 31 shall make the final funding decision on each application 32 and may approve, deny, defer, or modify each application, in 33 the board’s discretion, to fund as many events as possible 34 with the moneys available. The board and the authority may 35 -5- SF 660.2142 (2) 91 ns/js 5/ 10 negotiate with an eligible applicant regarding the details of 1 the applicant’s proposed event and the amount and terms of 2 any financial assistance. In making final funding decisions 3 pursuant to this subsection, the board and the authority shall 4 be exempt from chapter 17A. 5 (2) An application and staff evaluation forwarded to 6 the board under subsection 1 shall remain eligible for 7 consideration by the board under subparagraph (1) for up to two 8 years from the date of receipt of the application by the board. 9 b. In order to be awarded financial assistance under the 10 program, an applicant must demonstrate the ability to provide 11 matching funds for the event that equal at least fifty percent 12 of the award of financial assistance. 13 Sec. 10.
